Photograph: Alessio Mamo/The Guardian View image in fullscreen A Ukrainian military editor known by his call sign Catman edits footage taken by a Ukrainian kamikaze drone. Photograph: Alessio Mamo/The Guardian Ukraine ‘Our task is to laugh at these enemies’: the Ukrainian unit posting drone videos of Russian soldiers’ last moments Creators of chase compilations reject any moral qualms and say they show ‘death is waiting’ for those who join war Luke Harding in Kyiv Tue 18 Aug 2026 07.43 EDT Last modified on Tue 18 Aug 2026 08.26 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google T o many observers they will appear dehumanising and offensive. To many Ukrainians, however, they are a brutal reminder of the fate that awaits Russian soldiers who take part in Vladimir Putin’s invasion, as well as a potent propaganda weapon. Over the past year and a half, videos of kamikaze drones chasing Russian service personnel to their deaths have become a distinctive genre on social media. They are the brainchild of Robert Brovdi , the head of Ukraine’s unmanned systems forces and founder of “Magyar’s Birds” , named after his call sign. Brovdi’s 414th aviation strike brigade has pioneered the use of battlefield video, much of it recorded by first-person-view drones. The death videos are known as yoblyks , a portmanteau that combines the root of the Ukrainian for “fuck” with an affectionate diminutive form. The closest English translation is probably “fuckling”. An excerpt of footage from a drone following a Russian soldier into woodland Early each morning, a military editor known by his call sign Catman sifts through battlefield clips recorded the previous day, selecting some for a two-minute compilation and adding pulsing or mystical music. A longer online reel is titled “Yoblyks of the Week”. Defending his work, Catman said the videos played an important role in demoralising ordinary Russians and revealing the true cost of the Kremlin’s unprovoked war. “My goal is to show Russians that if they mobilise in Ukraine they will be killed, that it’s a one-way ticket and death is waiting for them,” he said. He acknowledged that the clips were deliberately arranged to mock the victims, who are sometimes seen throwing sticks at the drones to try to knock them off course, or falling over as they run. Though the moment of death is not shown, the last frame is a closeup of a soldier’s face. “We have a phrase: laughter kills fear. Our main task is to laugh at these enemies and to depict them as helpless. This boosts the morale of our forces,” he said. “It’s impossible for me to feel sorry for them. It’s war, after all, not a movie.” View image in fullscreen Catman sitting in front of his computer: ‘My goal is to show Russians that if they mobilise in Ukraine they will be killed.’ Photograph: Alessio Mamo/The Guardian Typically, the Russian soldiers are killed while walking or travelling by motorbike to the frontline. Some are unaware they are at risk from drones, Catman said, and appear to have been tricked by their commanders. “Their training is short. A lot die just two weeks after enlisting,” he said. He described most of the soldiers as “banal donkey men” ordered to carry provisions or fuel to exposed Russian positions. Others drag communication cables. Since February, when Elon Musk shut down his satellite internet service Starlink in Russia, officers in the rear have struggled to contact frontline units. Another member of Magyar’s Birds said there was compelling evidence the Russians were routinely misled about dangers. “You can see from the videos a lot of them are not even hiding,” he said. “They use their radio sets. A large number are fooled by the lie that everything will be OK, that they are going to their positions and are totally safe.” The brigade has an archive of about 3,600 videos. Only two feature women, both wearing combat uniform and carrying assault rifles. “There is no difference for me. They are all enemies,” Catman said. The videos play an important part in verifying Russian losses, which are running at more than 30,000 soldiers a month killed or injured, according to Kyiv. An excerpt of footage from a drone following a Russian soldier into a house Brovdi said he had no qualms about publishing material that many in the west might find distasteful and morally dubious. “God forbid they should ever experience pain. Because those of us in Ukraine who have experienced real physical pain from war would never agree with that perspective,” he said. In daily posts, Brovdi uses language that some might find gratuitous, for instance describing Russians as “worms” pecked by “birds”. He said: “When the war started, everything changed. There was a desire to humiliate the enemy as much as possible, not with typical words but exotic ones. It was only natural that military technical folklore and coinages such as ‘yoblyk’ found their way into my speech. They existed before AI.” View image in fullscreen Robert ‘Magyar’ Brovdi, the commander of Ukraine’s unmanned systems forces. Photograph: Alessio Mamo/The Guardian The videos have sparked several trolling subgenres. Some Russian women post photos of themselves saying farewell to their husbands as they leave to take part in what Putin calls a “special military operation”. Ukrainians identify the men and subsequently reply with drone footage showing their deaths. According to Catman, the yoblyks have a wide audience, including inside Russia. “There is very little information there about soldiers who go missing. Some people search and take screenshots. Mothers or wives then post messages saying something bad has happened to their loved ones,” he said. Putin’s recruiters scramble to avoid second mass mobilisation as Ukraine losses mount Read more Pro-war Russian bloggers post images on Telegram channels of Ukrainian soldiers dying in battle. Other videos show the killing of unarmed Ukrainian prisoners of war – a crime. The Russian internet includes AI-generated fakes that purport to show Ukrainian military personnel criticising their army leadership. Anatolii Loza, a Ukrainian volunteer who was captured and imprisoned by Russia and recently swapped, said he saw nothing wrong with yoblyks . “International law doesn’t apply to killing combatants on the field of battle,” he said. “The Russians come to shoot our soldiers and civilians. They are wearing uniform. They deserve their fate.” Loza’s wife, Olena, said attitudes inside Ukraine hardened after spring 2022, when Russian forces killed hundreds of civilians in the cities of Bucha and Mariupol, leaving their bodies on the streets. Of yoblyks , she said: “I don’t find these videos informative. I’m already furious with Russia.” At the HQ of Magyar’s Birds, Catman said black humour was essential during wartime. “It’s important for our own people to say we are not just surviving. We need to show we are flourishing and hitting back hard against the enemy.” Betrayal: Trump, Putin and the New Age of Conquest, by Luke Harding, is published on 27 August by Guardian Faber. https://www.politico.eu/article/european.text: BRUSSELS — The EU’s top diplomat has proposed giving the bloc’s own organized crime prosecutors responsibility for bringing cases against companies and individuals that help Russia get around sanctions and fuel its war in Ukraine. Kaja Kallas, the EU’s high representative for foreign affairs and security policy, suggested handing oversight of sanctions circumventions cases to the European Prosecutor’s Public Office (EPPO). The Luxembourg-based agency would investigate those shipping sensitive trade goods that could be used by Moscow’s war machine or laundering money for the Kremlin. Kallas floated the idea at a meeting with ambassadors from EU member countries on Wednesday, two diplomats with knowledge of the discussion said — although she stopped short of making concrete proposals at this stage. Advertisement Advertisement The measure would see prosecutors target those inside the bloc’s own borders who fall foul of strict rules about working with sanctioned Russian and Belarusian entities, or engage in banned transactions. Enforcement of EU sanctions has been held back by a patchwork of national laws and different approaches from prosecutors in the 27 capitals. EPPO is currently tasked with investigating and prosecuting serious organized crime, including money laundering, corruption and cross-border fraud. International sanctions enforcement would be a major addition to its remit. In July, the EU approved its 21st package of sanctions against Moscow since the start of its full-scale invasion of Ukraine, targeting oil and gas exports, financial services and crypto exchanges used to move money into its institutions. Kallas did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

https://www.delfi.lt/en/politics/we-will.text: Delfi EN Delfi Politics 2026.09.07 07:00 "We will see and hear even more": more than just the German brigade will be operating in Lithuania Greta Klimkaitė Source: Delfi EN Residents of Vilnius came to welcome the 45th German Armoured Brigade PHOTO: Andrius Ufartas | Delfi Follow Delfi on Google The German brigade is bringing substantial military capabilities to Lithuania and sending a clear message to Russia: it would begin fighting from the very first moment. Moreover, Germany’s capabilities are also seen as the best alternative should the United States decide to withdraw its troops from Europe. Gintaras Ažubalis says that the capabilities of the German brigade are more than ten times greater than those of the allied forces previously stationed here. "This is no longer a single battalion, as it was before, but five battalions, roughly speaking: three combat battalions, two support battalions and many other units that form an integral, organic part of the brigade. But I would like to emphasise that, over time, there will be more here, because the Germans will not send just one brigade. There will be air-defence elements and so on. This is a very, very serious capability," the reserve colonel says. The German Army’s 45th Armoured Brigade, comprising three manoeuvre battalions and all the necessary enablers, including combat-support and sustainment units, is being permanently relocated to Lithuania. Around 5,000 German military personnel and civilian employees will be transferred to Lithuania, serving in Rukla, Pabradė and other military facilities. They will also bring approximately 2,000 pieces of military equipment with them. "It is a heavy brigade, which is also extremely important. Despite all our internal discussions, that element remains as fundamental to warfare and NATO doctrine as it has always been. Redeploying it would be technically quite difficult if urgent reinforcements were required. The fact that the heavy element is being stationed here — and that we will soon have one of our own as well — is very good," says the former Lithuanian defence attaché in Germany. "We are moving into an entirely different security league," says Laurynas Kasčiūnas, deputy chair of the Seimas Committee on National Security and Defence and a former minister of national defence. According to him, when the full-scale invasion of Ukraine began, NATO adopted the principle of forward defence. "I think the Latvians and especially the Estonians are slightly envious of us because, for the time being, they do not have this kind of architecture in their planning. We are leading the way here. This is precisely the result and consequence of the decisions made in 2022–2023. < ...> With the brigade’s relocation, this effectively doubles the military presence in Lithuania. We should bear in mind that the brigade can operate autonomously, but, in principle, the German brigade will be an integral part of even larger forces based in Germany. For example, it will form part of a German division whose assigned forces, under NATO’s new-generation defence plans, would operate in the defence of Lithuania and our region. In other words, if you asked me which ally would play the largest role in Lithuania’s defence in the event of aggression, the answer would, of course, be Germany, and it is now developing its land forces," L. Kasčiūnas explains. A Message to Russia According to G. Ažubalis, the brigade’s permanent deployment in Lithuania sends Russia a message about the unity of the Alliance. He says Germany’s decisions are no coincidence either. "Let us not forget that the brigade is just 30 kilometres from the border, as is Vilnius. I do not think it is a coincidence that the Germans chose this particular location rather than somewhere that would be more convenient for them from a technical perspective, such as Rukla. It is, after all, a difficult location and a highly risky one in military terms," the reserve colonel says. "From a military perspective, the Russians remember the Germans very well and know them perfectly well, despite all the difficulties that every European country is generally experiencing. We are seeing more and more positive signs in Germany regarding its military — the Bundeswehr. The good news is that they have finally managed to cross that threshold in terms of staffing. The trends are positive, not negative. For the first time, the size of the Bundeswehr has exceeded 180,000 troops, and its ambitions are high. I have no doubt that Germany will become not only an economic and political power in Europe, but also a military power," G. Ažubalis says. He says that, in the event of an enemy attack, German forces would begin defending Lithuania immediately. "Those who are here will receive their orders, and the fighting here will begin from the first minute, for the very first inch, as planned. I have no doubt about that whatsoever. And if someone has doubts, there is nothing that can be done about it. Speaking purely as a soldier, I can reassure you once again: I have no doubts here. If, God forbid, that day dawns, we will all be in formation, and I trust them completely," the reserve colonel insists. It is also emphasised that Germany’s intelligence capabilities will be employed in Lithuania. "With the arrival of the Germans, we will see even more and hear even more. In other words, Germany’s entire intelligence apparatus will be concentrated here, both through its technical means and its personnel and capabilities, because it is very important to them that the brigade does not become a target of provocations here. They will certainly be working very seriously here. We should also bear in mind that some troops are arriving with their families, and some will live in Vilnius and Kaunas. You settle here; this is a long-term presence. Psychologically, this becomes territory where your own citizens are present. That is very important because of the entire psychological dimension — if necessary, they will defend it, because their citizens are here too," L. Kasčiūnas says. An Alternative to U.S. Troops L. Kasčiūnas says that the current political situation in Germany is favourable to Lithuania and to the deployment of the brigade. "We now have [Friedrich] Merz as chancellor and [Boris] Pistorius as minister. I believe I have described them in the press as probably the best possible tandem for our region and for Lithuania that Germany could have today. Of course, Germany’s political system is highly dynamic; we know what is happening on the right and what views exist there, but, for now, I certainly do not see any possibility of them taking control of the Bundestag in the next federal election. In any event, that is their affair. But what we have now — this symbiosis between the chancellor and the defence minister, a truly excellent defence minister with whom I have also had many opportunities to speak — gives us a genuinely excellent opportunity," L. Kasčiūnas says. According to the politician, investment in Germany’s armed forces, the Bundeswehr, is also important. "Where they were ten years ago and where they are now are incomparable. And where will they be in another ten years? Huge sums are now being [allocated] to satellites and to strengthening intelligence capabilities. And because they will be here, we will share in all of that as well," the interviewee points out. Moreover, he recalls that questions remain unanswered about whether U.S. troops will be stationed in Lithuania. "The apocalypse has not happened yet; I think the Americans are staying here. But if they withdraw somewhat, in one way or another, we must nevertheless bear in mind that Germany’s presence here is the best possible alternative, because this is inevitable given the full scale of its capabilities. Germany is the only country that can compensate for what the United States provides to NATO in Europe. Only the Germans can do that, with all due respect to our neighbours, whose capabilities are also growing — but Germany is Germany, because its GDP is €3.5 trillion. Considering what Germany can put together for the defence of Europe as a whole, our partnership with Germany is a truly wonderful thing," L. Kasčiūnas says. https://www.dw.com/en/uk-fighter-jets-to.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OUPj Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets to fly missions to protect Saudi Arabia from Houthi attacks [FILE: November 21, 2024] Image: Joan Valls/Urbanandsport/NurPhoto/picture alliance Advertisement Britain will deploy Royal Air Force Typhoon fighter jets to Saudi Arabia to help defend the kingdom against increasing attacks by Yemen's Houthi rebels, the UK government announced on Tuesday. The aircraft will protect Saudi cities and critical infrastructure from drones and missiles, the Ministry of Defense said. They will not carry out offensive strikes against Houthi targets in Yemen . "The continuing attacks from the Houthis on our ally Saudi Arabia are absolutely despicable," British Defense Secretary Wes Streeting said. He particularly condemned attacks on Riyadh's international airport, which has been targeted 20 times since the beginning of October. Riyadh's international airport has seen a string of attacks claimed by the Houthis Image: Social Media/REUTERS Strikes on the airport have killed at least 18 people and wounded hundreds this month, according to reports. What additional military support is Britain providing? The deployment follows a request from Saudi Arabia and expands military assistance announced by London in September. Britain will also send an Atlas A400M military transport aircraft and military advisers. It has extended its offer to provide air-to-air refueling for Saudi aircraft operating against the Houthis for another 90 days. The announcement comes as Yemen's civil war continues to escalate following the collapse of a years-long truce in September. Houthi attacks have increasingly targeted Saudi oil facilities and civilian infrastructure. The rebels have also imposed a naval blockade and attacked tankers, disrupting oil exports and pushing up energy prices. Houthi rebels have targeted oil facilities in Saudi Arabia too [PHOTO: October 3] Image: REUTERS Inside Yemen, authorities said a Houthi strike on Monday killed 58 people at a training camp for Saudi-backed government security forces. Saudi Arabia and the United States accuse Iran of supporting the Houthis, an allegation Tehran denies. How is the conflict affecting Saudi Arabia's economy? Saudi Arabia has postponed its flagship Future Investment Initiative conference, informally known as "Davos in the Desert," until 2027. The event, originally scheduled for October 26-29, was expected to attract leading international financiers. According to media reports, major banks and private equity firms had raised security concerns about attending the event. The conference is a key part of Saudi Arabia's efforts to attract foreign investment and diversify its economy away from oil. Marine Traffic/Handout via REUTERS Baltic Block Of Russian Grain May Open Black Sea, Latvia Says Bloomberg Total Views: 1773 October 17, 2026 By Milda Seputyte and Aaron Eglitis Oct 16, 2026 (Bloomberg) –Europe should block the transit of Russian grain through Baltic ports as that may force Moscow to seek ways to open trading on the Black Sea, Latvian Prime Minister Andris Kulbergs said. Russia and Ukraine have attacked each other’s ports, terminals and shipping infrastructure in the Black Sea, sharply cutting exports of key commodities such as grain . Moscow has diverted some of these grain shipments to Latvian and Lithuanian ports over rail, sparking criticism in the Baltic countries, which are European Union and NATO members. “It’s needed that we put the right pressure in order for Russia to understand that they need themselves to open the Black Sea,” Kulbergs said in an interview in Brussels on Friday. Ukraine needs to be able to sell its grain, to partly fill in the financing gap its facing this winter , he added.
